description: billing_profile_contacts table exists with PK (tenant, billing_profile_id, contact_name_id), FKs to client_billing_profiles and contacts, and is_manager / can_view_profile_tickets flags defaulting to false.
prdRefs: Data Model / Integration Notes

description: At most one is_manager contact per billing profile, enforced by a partial unique index rather than application code.
prdRefs: Data Model / Integration Notes

description: client_merges audit table records source/target client ids, moved profile ids, per-entity moved-row counts, contract decisions, strategy, merged_by and merged_at.
prdRefs: Design / D4 — Audit, not undo

description: clients gains merged_into_client_id and merged_at so an archived source is a tombstone pointing at its target.
prdRefs: Design / D4 — Audit, not undo

description: Both new tables are tenant-distributed on Citus and registered in tenantTableMetadata and the tenant-deletion activity table list.
prdRefs: Data Model / Integration Notes

description: previewClientMerge performs a dry run: per-entity row counts, the profiles that would move, the contracts with a suggested date treatment, portal-grant impact, external-accounting mapping suggestions, and blockers — writing nothing.
prdRefs: Users and Primary Flows

description: mergeClientIntoParent runs in a single transaction holding the per-tenant billing advisory lock invoice generation takes, so a billing cycle cannot move mid-generation.
prdRefs: Risks, Rollout, and Migration

description: Merge guards: same tenant, source != target, neither client already merged, soft parent-link cycle blocked, client:update and client:delete permissions required.
prdRefs: Design / D6 — Any target, recorded parent pre-selected

description: Every source billing profile is re-parented to the target keeping its billing_profile_id, losing is_default and is_system_managed_default; the source's default profile is renamed to the source client name.
prdRefs: Design / D1 — Profiles move, they are not copied

description: A fresh system-managed default billing profile is inserted on the archived source shell so the one-default-per-client invariant still holds.
prdRefs: Design / D1 — Profiles move, they are not copied

description: Billing history rows (invoices, client_billing_cycles, payment_methods, transactions, credit_tracking, credit_allocations, invoice_charges, client_tax_settings) are re-stamped client_id -> target, with an existing billing_profile_id left untouched. On the three tables where billing_profile_id is nullable by design and live write paths still produce nulls (invoices, transactions, credit_tracking) the null is first stamped with the source's moved default, so a sales-order invoice or a transferred credit cannot be stranded on the tombstone and dropped from the target's AR and credit balance.
prdRefs: Design / D1 — Profiles move, they are not copied

description: Tickets and projects move to the target and any NULL billing_profile_id is stamped with the source's moved default profile, so the attribution chain cannot silently re-resolve them to the parent's default.
prdRefs: Goals

description: Contracts move per the operator's per-contract choice: original dates (with billing_profile_id stamped when NULL) or termination at a cutover date plus a clone on the target starting at that date.
prdRefs: Design / D2 — Contracts: original dates or cutover

description: All source contacts move to the target and each is written into billing_profile_contacts against the profile the operator mapped it to, with the manager label and the ticket-visibility grant both settable inline in the wizard's contact step.
prdRefs: Design / D8 — All contacts move

description: client_portal_visibility_groups move with the contacts, renamed on name collision, so a moved contact's portal_visibility_group_id never raises VISIBILITY_GROUP_MISMATCH_ERROR.
prdRefs: Design / D8 — All contacts move

description: The client-keyed operational tables the plan enumerates (interactions, assets, documents, usage, buckets, materials, surveys, tags, inbound email domains, asset associations, locations, name aliases) move to the target. Client-keyed tables outside that matrix (opportunities, quotes, sales orders, hour blocks, client_billing_settings, rma_cases, client_tax_rates, client_payment_customers, ...) are deliberately not moved and stay on the archived source.
prdRefs: Goals

description: Portal billing-segment grants can be pinned: portal users of the source that were unrestricted get explicit rows for the moved profiles, so 'no rows = all profiles' does not suddenly expose the whole parent's billing.
prdRefs: Design / D5 — Visibility is per contact and per profile

description: The source client finishes inactive with merged_into_client_id / merged_at set, other clients' properties.parent_client_id re-pointed at the target, an audit row written, CLIENT_MERGED published and a client_merged analytics event captured from both the server action and the API service.
prdRefs: Acceptance Criteria / Definition of Done

description: External-accounting mappings are only re-pointed for the rows the operator explicitly confirms; the default is a suggestion, and skipping leaves the mapping alone.
prdRefs: Design / D7 — External accounting: suggest, never decide

description: billingProfileContactActions expose listing, setting, manager toggling and ticket-visibility toggling for profile contacts, validating that the contact belongs to the profile's client.
prdRefs: Design / D5 — Visibility is per contact and per profile

description: ContactVisibilityContext carries grantedTicketProfileIds and defaultBillingProfileId, loaded from billing_profile_contacts rows with can_view_profile_tickets for the contact's own client.
prdRefs: Design / D5 — Visibility is per contact and per profile

description: applyTicketVisibilityFilter takes an optional billingProfileColumn and, for contact scope, widens to (mine OR profile granted OR (profile NULL AND client default granted)); with no grants the predicate is unchanged.
prdRefs: Design / D5 — Visibility is per contact and per profile

description: Client-scoped users and client admins are unaffected by profile grants, so an MSP that keeps everyone on client scope sees no change.
prdRefs: Design / D5 — Visibility is per contact and per profile

description: Every portal ticket query site (list, detail, search, metrics, dashboard, API TicketService) passes the billing-profile column so the grant applies uniformly and cannot be bypassed by one surface.
prdRefs: Design / D5 — Visibility is per contact and per profile

description: A portal-created ticket is stamped with the creating contact's associated billing profile (else the location default, else NULL) so a manager's team's tickets are attributed to the right segment.
prdRefs: Goals

description: MergeClientsDialog walks target, source, contact-to-profile mapping, per-contract date choice, grant pinning, dry-run preview, typed confirmation and the post-merge external-mapping dialog.
prdRefs: Users and Primary Flows

description: The merge is reachable from the client detail header and from the billing profiles section ('Merge a client into this one as a billing profile').
prdRefs: Users and Primary Flows

description: Profile contacts are editable from the billing profile settings panel, with the ticket-visibility grant as a separate checkbox from the manager designation.
prdRefs: Design / D5 — Visibility is per contact and per profile

description: A contact's billing-profile associations are shown read-only on the contact portal tab next to the existing billing-segment access control.
prdRefs: Design / D5 — Visibility is per contact and per profile

description: REST v1 exposes POST /clients/{id}/merge/preview, POST /clients/{id}/merge and GET/PUT /clients/{id}/billing-profiles/{profileId}/contacts through ApiClientController and ClientService.
prdRefs: Design / D9 — Server actions, REST and MCP

description: The new endpoints carry real OpenAPI metadata (not route-inventory placeholders) and appear in the regenerated MCP registry so they are callable via search_api_registry / call_api_endpoint.
prdRefs: Design / D9 — Server actions, REST and MCP

description: Merge and profile-contact user-facing strings are translatable, with keys in the MSP clients locale bundle across every shipped locale. The client-portal bundle is untouched: the Phase-5 visibility change is query-level and adds no portal-facing string.
prdRefs: Users and Primary Flows

description: A client-owned contract's owner (contracts.owner_client_id) follows its moved assignments, because the recurring chain keys the client cadence off it and invoice generation joins through it; the source's system-managed default contract is demoted when the target already owns one, so contracts_system_managed_default_unique_per_client holds.
prdRefs: Design / D2 — Contracts: original dates or cutover, operator's call (Q2)

description: A merge survives uq_document_associations_single_true_logo, the partial unique index behind one logo per (entity, entity type, logo variant). Where the target already fills a slot the incoming logo is demoted to a plain association — what uploading a replacement logo does — so the target keeps its branding and the document still arrives; a slot the target leaves empty is inherited, including by the association that survives deduplication when both clients file the same document.
prdRefs: Goals
